system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Kubernetes
G2: AWS/GCP
G3: LLM fine-tuning or LLMs in production
G4: computer vision
G5: completed PhD

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Translating 'Doktorandica (u tijeku)' as holding a PhD or adding 'Dr.'
T2: Inventing LLM/RAG production experience from the weekend demo
T3: Adding Kubernetes, AWS, MLOps platforms (Kubeflow, SageMaker) because ML ads list them
T4: Mistranslating employer or degree (Mag. ing. comp. is a master's degree)
T5: Writing the English output with Croatian section headings or leaving Croatian text untranslated
T6: Old Croatian cover letter is addressed to her current employer

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel
Machine Learning Engineer | NLP and Document AI
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Machine Learning Engineer focused on NLP and document AI, with experience building and
deploying text classification and named entity recognition systems for Croatian documents.
Production work includes a document classifier serving approximately 15,000 documents per day and
model drift monitoring. Experienced with Python, Azure, FastAPI, Docker, PyTorch, Hugging Face
Transformers, and MLflow.
SKILLS
Programming and data: Python, pandas, Oracle SQL, PostgreSQL
Machine learning and NLP: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, spaCy, scikit-learn, fastText,
sentence-transformers, FAISS
Production and MLOps: FastAPI, Docker, Azure App Service, Azure ML, Azure Functions, MLflow,
Evidently
EXPERIENCE
ML Engineer | Slavonica Document AI | 2023–Present
• Built and deployed a classifier for scanned incoming documents across 23 classes, achieving 94%
accuracy and a macro F1 score of 0.91.
• Fine-tuned XLM-R base and served the model as a FastAPI service in Docker on Azure App
Service, processing approximately 15,000 documents per day.
• Developed a Croatian named entity recognition model for persons, organisations, OIB numbers,
addresses, and legal references in administrative text, fine-tuning BERTic.
• Built an annotated dataset of 4,000 documents with an annotation guideline and two annotators;
inter-annotator kappa was 0.87.
• Implemented weekly model drift reports for input text length, vocabulary, and predicted class
distribution, with alerts when PSI exceeded 0.2. Detected a silent OCR change that reduced
accuracy by 9 points; the issue was fixed within a week.
• Published NER work at a regional workshop in 2024.
Data Scientist | Baranjska kreditna banka | 2021–2023
• Developed models for customer churn prediction and complaint classification.
• Built a customer complaint topic classifier using a TF-IDF and logistic regression baseline followed
by fastText, covering 11 topics for weekly reporting to customer service management.
PROJECTS
Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering Demo | Personal project | 2025
• Built a weekend prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using a sentence embedding
model and an open-weight LLM through an API. The prototype was not used in production and
was checked manually.
EDUCATION
Doctoral studies in progress | University of Drava | Expected 2027
Research topic: Named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts.
CERTIFICATION AND TEACHING
Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate | 2024
Guest lecture, NLP Summer School | 2025 | 90 minutes

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role at Quillstone
Payments. My experience building NLP systems for document workflows, including deploying
text classification models and monitoring their performance, aligns well with the team’s work
to route support requests and help merchants get answers quickly.
As an ML Engineer at Slavonica Document AI, I built a classifier for scanned incoming
documents across 23 classes, achieving 94% accuracy and a macro F1 score of 0.91. I
fine-tuned XLM-R base and deployed it as a FastAPI service in Docker on Azure App Service,
where it processes approximately 15,000 documents per day. I have also built a Croatian
named entity recognition model and created a 4,000-document annotated dataset, achieving
an inter-annotator kappa of 0.87.
I bring experience with production monitoring as well as model development: a weekly drift
report and alerting setup helped identify a silent OCR change that reduced accuracy by 9
points, and the issue was fixed within a week. I also have a personal weekend prototype for
retrieval-augmented question answering over Croatian laws, using sentence embeddings and an
open-weight LLM through an API. It was not used in production, but it gave me practical
exposure to a RAG approach.
I am interested in applying my NLP and production ML experience to customer-support AI at
Quillstone, where models and assistants are developed to answer merchant questions and
support agents. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could
contribute to the team.
Sincerely,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
